messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: serving-prod - ALERT: CUDA_ILLEGAL_MEMORY_ACCESS spike on node gpu-23. Error rate >5% across serving-runtime pods. Triage channel created.

sre-joe: Oncall here. Seeing repeated container restarts on gpu-23 starting ~14:01 UTC, correlated with a model reload. Pulling logs now.

runtime-kate: I grabbed the pod logs and a kernel oops from the node. Container exit: `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` inside attention kernel during KV cache restore. Attaching dmesg snippet below.

runtime-kate: ```
[  123.456789] NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[  123.457001] kernel: [drm] nvrm: illegal device address at 0x7f8a1b2c3d40
[  123.457203] python[21456]: terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
[  123.457204] python[21456]:   what():  CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS
```

eng-ml-ana: We pushed a rolling model reload at ~14:01 (warmup + KV restore + 8 concurrent warmup lanes). If a preemption or page migration happened during the memcpy/kv swap, pointer base could shift.

deploy-bot: rollback job started: rolling back serving-runtime image -> v1.42.2-stable.

sre-joe: Cordon+drain on gpu-23 in progress, evicted affected pods, and forced failover to other GPU nodes. Network traffic routed to fallback pool.

incident-bot: CUSTOMER IMPACT: Approximately 5% of requests in us-west1 saw failures (500s) tied to these pods; auto-fallback to smaller model triggered for new incoming requests to reduce failed rate.

cust-success-zoe: Notified impacted accounts (two mid-size customers) with initial blurb. CS will follow up with postmortem once we have root cause. :white_check_mark:

runtime-kate: Repro steps on dev: `./serve --model reload --concurrent=8` + trigger preemption (kill -9 of helper thread) reproduces illegal-address reliably on our dev GPU. Hypothesis: KV swap does async GPU memcpy and doesn't synchronize with device memory layout update -> stale pointer used after a page migration.

eng-ml-ana: Quick mitigation we can test: add `cudaDeviceSynchronize()` and guard the KV pointer update behind a host-side fence. I'll compile a canary and smoke test.

oncall-miguel: Taking follow-up handoff in 30m. Current mitigations in place: cordon gpu-23, rollback to v1.42.2-stable, enable CPU fallback for affected customer routes. Anything else I should know?

sre-joe: No blockers from infra. Core dumps + logs are in /mnt/incident-artifacts/7654321000 and uploaded to the incident bucket s3://redwood-incidents/7654321000/. Leaving notes on runbook steps we tried.

oncall-miguel: ACK. Assigning to runtime-kate + eng-ml-ana for the root cause and hotfix PR. I'll monitor through the night and escalate to kernel/driver team if kernel oops recurs.

incident-bot: STATUS: mitigation ongoing, severity downgraded to mitigated. Will update when hotfix is deployed and fully validated.

runtime-kate: Quick follow-up: collect `nvidia-smi -q` and `dmesg -T` if you repro; also capture the full `core.*` from crashed container. Those helped us pinpoint the memcpy window.

eng-ml-ana: I'll open a PR with the guard + test and request a staged rollout to canary before wide deploy.

oncall-miguel: Handoff complete. I'm the active oncall. Monitoring channel: #incidents. Ping me for any regressions.
